title: Padsevonil in WWOX-LoF
summary: Separate synaptic target binding from recruitment of inhibition.

graph.evidence: Adult PET showed high SV2A occupancy. Phase 3 did not confirm the efficacy endpoints.
graph.inference: Occupancy alone cannot establish balanced inhibitory and excitatory release.
graph.hypothesis: A brief GABA-A effect could restore inhibitory recruitment at matched SV2A engagement.
graph.experiment: Measure native inhibitory output with benzodiazepine-site blockade and matched SV2A engagement.

evidence: The highest phase 3 arm had 8/56 responders on the 75% endpoint versus 7/54 on placebo. Somnolence was 20/59 versus 2/55 in the corresponding safety sets.
inference: Trial whole-blood troughs and a published blood/plasma comparison support near-saturation scenarios for SV2A in the highest phase 2b arm. Direct trial occupancy and functional GABA-A coverage remain uncertain.
hypothesis: A useful brief GABA-A contribution could preserve recruitment when presynaptic release is modified. A later response could instead reflect SV2 residence or other SV2 isoforms.
experiment: Compare padsevonil with brivaracetam at measured, matched SV2A engagement. Test whether benzodiazepine-site blockade removes any gain in inhibitory recruitment and preserve the first excitatory response as a control.
limits: Retain as a conditional ex vivo comparator and defer pediatric WWOX priority. Adult results leave juvenile exposure, recruitment and developmental outcomes unresolved.
